title: Codex skill parity remediation
task_summary: Create an evidence-bearing, custody-safe Codex skill projection system and close the audited discoverability gaps without duplicating canonical authority.
scope_justification: The task changes repository-local Codex skill discovery, adapter policy, projection tooling, validation, and derived harness instructions.
description: Remediate the full Codex skill parity audit by defining explicit projection policy, generating reviewed-safe missing projections, repairing invalid or stale projections only under bounded custody, and verifying real Codex discovery and capability truth.
requested_by: operator via $bp-r with explicit instruction to plan and run

similarity_assessment.match_rationale: The framework covers cross-harness standardization and runtime normalization, but the concrete Codex projection and custody mechanics are bespoke gaps.
gaps: No existing prompt chain owns Codex skill candidate generation or Codex frontmatter normalization
No existing framework defines direct versus routed exposure for framework-local helpers
No existing framework establishes path-level custody for the current untracked .agents tree

existing_work_check.disposition: False-positive and subset matches only. Framework registry, lifecycle mechanics, ticktock, and outward/inward plans do not own the umbrella Codex projection surface; this plan adopts only the current lifecycle slice and does not overwrite their Claude sources.

lessons: Worker-green is insufficient; reverify in the real harness
Untracked status does not prove custody
Generated projections remain derivative of canonical or accepted source authority

steps.stage_title: Prove and declare the projection contract
steps.description: Run this and all later implementation steps in the isolated worktree `~/.mythos-worktrees/mythos-codex-skill-parity-remediation` on branch `codex/skill-parity-remediation`, after copying only the adopted lifecycle and blueprint artifacts into that worktree. Adopt the existing lifecycle slice as probation evidence; add explicit, machine-consumed projection families and capability tiers to the Codex adapter; implement one general projector with separate canonical-command, direct-system-skill, alias-resolution, and framework-helper strategies; derive deterministic handler coverage from the exported HANDLERS registry; preserve the lifecycle script as a compatibility wrapper; stamp candidates and receipts with generator id, source path, source hash, projection kind, capability tier, and semantic review state. UNKNOWN, harness-specific, malformed, colliding, or private-path-bearing candidates must be staged and rejected from application. Include negative fixtures for ground-in-philosophy's Pi-specific semantics, adapter-managed commands without HANDLERS (must be ADVISORY rather than BLOCKING), alias cycles/nonterminal targets, and aliases such as tt/oil/chi that cross the command-to-project-skill boundary.
steps.framework_step: meta/execution-normalization: runtime contract extraction and cross-harness standardization

steps.stage_title: Project reviewed-safe capabilities in bounded families
steps.description: From the isolated worktree, run the projector in candidate mode, review classifications, then apply only proven-absent and reviewed-safe outputs into that same worktree's `.agents/skills`. Prioritize daily operator vocabulary and governance: go, ticktock/tt, owl/oa/dl/oc resolution, ground-in-philosophy, repair-plan, and sm-os-status. Project the remaining safe canonical command pointers and the four missing direct skills from current accepted Claude sources. Resolve aliases dynamically through command-aliases and prove resolution; do not duplicate alias behavior. Project framework-local helpers only under a collision-free guild-<service>-<framework>-<skill> namespace with lineage and guardrail references. Repair the 33 invalid and 69 drift-candidate existing packages only in path-bounded child batches that preserve bodies/resources and have explicit custody evidence; otherwise record them as blocked residuals rather than overwrite them.
steps.framework_step: meta/execution-normalization: staged normalization and reviewed application
files_touched: .agents/skills/<custody-approved existing projections>/SKILL.md (EDIT only after exact-path preflight)

steps.stage_title: Verify real harness behavior and close through review
steps.description: From the same isolated worktree, run projector check mode, pinned Codex package-schema validation, canonical and alias resolution coverage, lifecycle tests, negative fixtures, path-leak checks, and instructions generation/validation after generated-output custody is secured. Produce separate counts for present, syntactically valid, resolvable, semantically reviewed, deterministic-handler-backed, and UNKNOWN. Obtain fresh Codex runtime receipts using `codex exec --ephemeral --sandbox read-only -C ~/.mythos-worktrees/mythos-codex-skill-parity-remediation --output-last-message <receipt> <probe>` for at least one direct skill, canonical command skill, alias, and framework helper; if the CLI cannot expose or invoke a class, report that class as discovery UNKNOWN. Inspect the scoped diff, run a distinct-family acceptance review bound to the diff and receipts, repair blocking findings through an amendment, then produce a debrief. Perform the commit/PR leg only in this worktree on branch `codex/skill-parity-remediation`; if worktree privacy or identity gates prevent scoped staging/review, stop at an explicit operator gate rather than changing the shared checkout.
files_touched: AGENTS.md and other generator-owned outputs only through npm run instructions:generate

required_gates: No existing .agents skill overwrite without exact-path custody and content-preserving strategy
UNKNOWN or harness-specific candidates cannot be applied without a reviewed Codex override
Aliases resolve dynamically and never become independent behavioral authority
Presence, package validity, semantic review, runtime resolution, and deterministic enforcement are reported separately
Consequence-grade plan review and distinct-family implementation review are required
Scoped commit and PR must exclude unrelated dirty work and run only from the declared secondary worktree
expected_outcomes: A machine-consumed Codex projection contract and one source-family-aware projector exist
All audited missing capabilities are either projected with receipts or explicitly classified UNKNOWN/unsupported with a named blocker
The four missing direct skills and reviewed-safe missing canonical commands are available to Codex without copied canonical authority
Alias parity is mechanically proven without behavior duplication
Framework-local helper exposure is explicit and lineage-preserving
Existing invalid or stale skills are repaired only where custody is proven; all residuals are enumerated
Real-harness receipts and independent review support every parity claim
A feature-branch PR contains only this workstream's files
bounded_plan.risk_notes: High cross-harness and multi-actor risk. The main falsifiers are a generated skill that contains false-for-Codex semantics, a capability marked deterministic without a registered handler, an alias body that diverges from its target, a framework helper detached from lineage/guardrails, a write to a foreign existing skill, or a discovery claim supported only by file presence. Any of these blocks acceptance.
bounded_plan.hardening_opportunity: If successful, register the projector's coverage check as the Codex parity gate and retire lifecycle-only duplication after its probation evidence is reviewed.

routing_expectations.review_lane_rationale: This is cross-harness system work spanning policy, generators, many projected packages, and actual Codex discovery. Local tests are necessary but insufficient; distinct-family review and consequence-grade convene evidence are required.
escalation_triggers: Any inability to distinguish an existing file's custody
Any candidate classified UNKNOWN or containing another harness's capability claim
Any need to overwrite unrelated dirty work or change branches in the shared checkout
Any real-harness discovery failure despite passing package validation

scope_identity.working_surface: /Users/admin/mythos for blueprint artifacts; ~/.mythos-worktrees/mythos-codex-skill-parity-remediation for all implementation, validation, commit, and PR work
forbidden_artifacts: all unrelated dirty or untracked paths
scope_identity.dynamic_ownership_rule: A generated .agents/skills path enters this workstream's owned set only after the projector emits a receipt naming that exact path, proves it absent immediately before write, and classifies the candidate reviewed-safe. An existing path requires a CustodyRecord containing the exact path, preflight git status, SHA-256 of current bytes, attribution source (generator stamp or UNKNOWN), and an operator-stamp reference. UNKNOWN attribution or a missing operator stamp blocks refresh and leaves the file as an enumerated residual.

prior_reviews.disposition: All blocking architecture adjustments incorporated before this plan was written.
